description: Node CPU microbenchmark comparing the former full-buffer frontend recomputation and exact cumulative-audio append on every streaming chunk with the incremental X-ASR frontend and amortized audio backing buffer. It reports both a frontend-only control and the combined shipped path; neither is an end-to-end transcription RTFx claim.

runtime.hardware: local Windows workstation; CPU model not captured

method.baseline: append each chunk to a growing Float32Array and run frontend.process() over the complete accumulated audio
method.candidate: append each chunk through the same amortized backing-buffer strategy used by the executor, then run frontend.processIncremental() over only newly stable frames with a bounded 400-sample tail; flush reflected boundary frames once with final=true
method.correctness: candidate features are compared with one full-buffer process() result; max absolute error must be < 1e-6

caveats: The logical cumulative audio view remains available for stream metadata while capacity growth is amortized; retained capacity can exceed the logical length until stream disposal.
End-to-end X-ASR encoder and decoder timing must be remeasured on a real artifact before claiming an RTFx improvement.
Right-edge reflected frames are intentionally delayed until the next chunk or finalization to preserve full-buffer parity.
